problem.title: Redis Key Format Migration Causing Cache Miss Avalanches
problem.prompt: Developer changing Redis cache key convention from 'user:101' to 'v2:user:101' in a new software release.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Never alter live cache key naming schemes without implementing dual- read fallback or pre-warming to prevent cache avalanches."

Production Hardening: Implement Dual-Read / Lazy-Migration: v2 code checks 'v2:user:101'; if missing, it checks fallback key 'user:101' and migrates the key forward asynchronously, or pre-warm new keys
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.
constraints: Incident Scenario Baseline: Developer changing Redis cache key convention from 'user:101' to 'v2:user:101' in a new software release.
Failure Cascade Path: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown
Sub-millisecond rejection / shed latency for overloaded requests

Breakdown Chain: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown
